brief: Tech outperformed last week and reclaimed its 50 and 100 day moving averages amid rate hike and oil volatility concerns plus AI debates over regulation, safety and agentic commerce. Breadth stayed narrow and sentiment cautious despite the move. Communacopia conference feedback was bullish for Tech and AI, yet the AI infrastructure trade still has not regained momentum despite several positive catalysts (ROIC commentary, model updates, easing technicals), raising the question of whether semiconductor weakness (SOX forward P/E near multi year lows) is a macro problem tied to oil or an AI problem. The market keeps rewarding asset light, AI levered 'inference economy' names and has expanded multiples for longer duration names like NET and SNOW even as 10 year yields hit multi decade highs. GS GIR notes on Microsoft describe three capex decisions now paying off, front loaded long dated capex, 1P/3P balancing that lifted Copilot and MAI quality, and frontier/enterprise balancing that left the entire $51bn Q4 RPO increase enterprise sourced, though Microsoft's forward P/E stays below its 10 year average. AMAT stays rated HOLD as memory cycle and 2027 discovery value debates de-rate its multiple, even as the stock bounced off its 200 day average.
